brief: Speed up CUDA prefill of the 35B (Qwen3.6-35B-A3B NVFP4) on GB10 by speeding up the routed-expert MoE prefill kernel (41-47 % of prefill kernel time at 22-33 % of the bf16 roof), keeping the default accumulation order and every accuracy bar; profile with nsys first; opt-in flag, draft PR.
hypothesis: The expert grouped GEMM is limited by schedule (tiling, occupancy, dequant/MMA overlap, launch structure), not by arithmetic, so a better schedule with the same accumulation order should speed it up without touching the kernel error.

summary: Opt-in INTARSIA_CUDA_MOE_W4A16_PF=1: L2 prefetch of block scales and packed weights in the gate/up half of the w4a16 MoE kernel plus a 64-row tile, for chunks up to 2048 tokens. Bitwise the default output, so no accuracy bar moved. Kernel -7 % / -4 % at 1k / 2k tokens; prefill +7 % at 1k, +1 % at 4k, +0.6 to +4 % at 16k against main with lt on; decode unchanged. The kernel is DRAM-stream bound at 1k and y/combine bound at 4k; about ten other bitwise schedule changes gave nothing.
lessons: With the compute ablated, the w4a16 expert kernel still took 93 % (1k) of its time: it is a weight-stream kernel at prefill chunk sizes of a few thousand tokens, so the lever is the memory pipeline, not the MMA schedule.
A cap on a prefetch knob must be tested on the first size above it: 2560 tokens was 3 % slower with the cap at 80 pairs per expert.
A stamped build is needed for acc-short: the first gate run failed on the missing INTARSIA_BUILD_STAMP; use scripts/tree-stamp.sh output.
